title: I made a game about finding one straw among 18,304 needles
author: wannabestraight
selftext:
I thought it would be funny to see what came up if i asked AI to do a incremental game with a really common theme (Needle in a haystack etc) but invert the prompt, asked DeepSeek Flash to construct the game out of that decription only, and gave it no style direction other than to "write a bit of lore" 

  
Well i sure as hell got lore, and tons of it,with absolute bangers like "The god did not die. It was combed" which im pretty sure is deepseek misunderstanding my "make insane amount of lore" as "make insane lore" 

The games premise is simple, you have 18,304 needles and a single straw. find the straw. 

Expected something barely working (given DeepSeek said after 67 minutes that it was done, having costed only 1.56$ in API costs) and was skeptical but ended up playing it for like 20 minutes, got massively excited that i actually managed to find the straw, only for Deepseek to crush my dreams by telling me it was a bug and then blatantly wiping my progress (who knew LLMs can be assholes)..

 Now i really wanna push this game further and make the multiplayer work properly etc. and maybe add stuff to drop just enough lore to the player that they keep ripping out needles without getting bored, but never feeling quite satisfied enough to stop.

  
I also like the fact that DeepSeek flash is clearly trained on a lot of game material, given it made the titlescreen essentially be "TEMU Elden Ring" (not even essentially, like its literally the composition of elden ring main menu lmao) 

  
If you wanna waste some minutes out of your life plucking needles out of a wall, [you can do so here](https://origozero.ai/world/Deata/hay-in-needlestack)

(For clarity, It was created in my game engine Zero, all source code is shared if your into reading that (might contain some absolute bangers) and you can make your own version by pressing the fork button. but thats enough self advertizement.)

This was honstly the first incremental game i actually played, and now i get why they sell like hot cakes, they are really addictive.

replies.author: wannabestraight
replies.body:
its not though ;\_; its rust + luau

I do see why one would think that though, when i made the UI systems for the engine, i modelled them after writing css and html, so while luau, it has full css parity meaning basically anything you can make on the web, you can make there the same way, so alot of the ui tends to end up looking like what you see in three.js games, since we just utilize the agents being already trained very heavily on css and html

replies.author: wannabestraight
replies.body:
Its not three.js based, i dont particularily like javascript so didnt want to go that route, i do like rust though, so its in rust, but scriptable in luau.

If you are interested to see how it works, essentially over 50% of the engines source code is luau and fully readable here [https://origozero.ai/world/Deata/builtin-library](https://origozero.ai/world/Deata/builtin-library) (or in engine, since well, the engine has its own virtual filesystem so you can just read the scripting side trough there too) 

For more info [https://origozero.ai/docs](https://origozero.ai/docs)
